hops.title: Why a fruit fly walls its brain off from its own blood
hops.text: A fruit fly's blood, its hemolymph, is rich in potassium: about 36 to 40 millimolar in classic measurements on larvae, roughly ten times the level in mammalian blood. More potassium outside pushes the resting voltage up in the GHK equation, and a large, lasting depolarization can leave neurons unable to fire. So the fly wraps its nervous system in a sheet of subperineurial glia sealed by septate junctions, which keeps the fluid in its brain at about 5 millimolar or less. Embryos missing neurexin IV, a protein of that seal, are paralyzed: their barrier breaks down and hemolymph potassium reaches the nerves.

sources.citation: Limmer S, Weiler A, Volkenhoff A, Babatz F, Klämbt C (2014). The Drosophila blood-brain barrier: development and function of a glial endothelium. Frontiers in Neuroscience 8:365.
Baumgartner S, Littleton JT, Broadie K, et al. (1996). A Drosophila neurexin is required for septate junction and blood-nerve barrier formation and function. Cell 87(6):1059-1068.

image.caption: Fly blood is rich in potassium, so a sealed glial barrier keeps the fluid around its brain low in potassium.

hops.afterHeading: A nudge takes time: the RC membrane
hops.title: Why a light pinch comes before a firm one
hops.text: Pinch a sheet of paper lightly between thumb and finger, then press harder with the same pinch. As the force rises, the working muscles call in stronger motor units, and input resistance does much of the sorting. The motor neurons driving small, weak units are smaller, and their membrane is also less leaky per square centimeter, so they leak less in total and have a higher input resistance. When a shared synaptic drive reaches the pool, Ohm's law hands those small cells the bigger voltage change, so they reach threshold first. That is Henneman's size principle: the weak units fire first, and the strong ones join as the drive grows.

sources.citation: Hug F, Avrillon S, Ibáñez J, Farina D (2023). Common synaptic input, synergies and size principle: Control of spinal motor neurons for movement generation. Journal of Physiology 601(1):11-20.
Gustafsson B, Pinter MJ (1984). Relations among passive electrical properties of lumbar alpha-motoneurones of the cat. Journal of Physiology 356:401-431.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: The same thumb-and-finger pinch on a sheet of paper shown twice, once light and relaxed, once pressing firmly.
image.caption: Small motor neurons have higher input resistance, so the same drive fires them first: light before firm.

hops.afterHeading: A nudge fades with distance: the cable
hops.title: The undersea telegraph cable behind cable theory
hops.text: On August 5, 1858, ships finished laying the first telegraph cable across the Atlantic. Queen Victoria's greeting to President Buchanan, under a hundred words, took more than 16 hours to get through, and within weeks the cable went dead. An inquiry blamed chief electrician Edward Whitehouse, whose huge induction coils were held to have broken down its gutta-percha insulation. The physicist William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin, had already worked out how pulses spread and blur along such a cable. In 1946 Alan Hodgkin and William Rushton used cable theory, now with a membrane leak, on a crustacean nerve fiber. That leak, against the core's resistance, sets a dendrite's length constant.

sources.citation: National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, Magnet Academy. Transatlantic Telegraph Cable – 1858.
Potgieter P, Linde L, van Blerk P, Birkill C, Fourie C (2025). High-frequency signals: a comparison between the cable equation and telegrapher's equations in nerves. BMC Biomedical Engineering 7:6.
Hodgkin AL, Rushton WAH (1946). The electrical constants of a crustacean nerve fibre. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B 133(873):444-479.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A historic ship paying out a black telegraph cable into Atlantic waves, with a cut piece of cable on deck.
image.caption: Cable theory began with an undersea telegraph cable; adding a membrane leak made it the math of dendrites.
